spec_interpretations: Section 6.50 and Figure 6 govern default RET_SUP_COR normal-storage destruction; Table 10 PARTIAL_CORRUPT wording conflicts with this default and Figure 6 reserves that transition for NO_RET_SUP_COR.

Balloon RTC does not freeze normal clocks while primary is NORMAL. Level controls transfer at the raw asserted-predicate trailing event, qualified using the condition at that event; condition-only changes do not manufacture transfers.

Level restore overrides older pending activations and their current-step NBA updates. The zero/future NBA distinction is an implementation inference from 6.50 priority and LRM 4.9.4; source-ordered later clock publications and positive-delay writes remain valid.

Exempt initial writes and direct own-state readbacks use normal storage; independently inferred outputs require primary and retention power under default RET_SUP_COR. Saved storage starts corrupt until an actual save.

completed.architecture: Preserve each parameter family as an optional setting until command updates and composite fanout validate; emit effective typed booleans defaulting to true. Opposite explicit settings conflict; omissions and empty lists add no setting. Balloon saved-only destruction does not advance normal-write epochs, and restore reads effective corrupt saved data without forwarding a concurrent save. Master NO_RET_SUP_COR permits normal writes behind an unpowered RET-driven output: reuse two existing independently guarded bounded NBA transactions, preserving every visible occurrence and retaining due-time eligibility across output-supply pulses. Functional and accepted initial own-state readbacks use typed normal-storage views; a shared compiler-only call-closure check handles static/direct class helpers and diagnoses unsupported state readbacks or opaque virtual dispatch. No new runtime API, opcode or service is introduced, and the special master path avoids an unused visibility state slot.
spec_interpretations: Section 6.50 limits NO_RET_SUP_COR to normal storage; Figure 6 PARTIAL_CORRUPT supports loss of an unpowered balloon with normal storage preserved. This topology-specific rule resolves the conditional retained-value wording in 9.7.2(a).

Master corruption follows Table 11: primary-ON/retention-OFF rows are qualified by RET_SUP_COR, but the both-OFF row unconditionally corrupts shared backing. Figure 7 omits that both-OFF exception under NO_RET_SUP_COR.

SAV_RES_COR qualifies overlap corruption for both balloon stores; disabling it does not disable real save/restore transfers, level-restore priority or independent power/RTC corruption. It has no operational effect for master/slave without save/restore controls.
Section 6.50 applies the physical retention-supply simstate to a retention-powered output even when NO_RET_SUP_COR preserves its primary-powered normal state. Ordinary outputs remain primary-powered.

The PON/ROFF normal-initialization/output-mask case is verified. Broader ordering of master initialization and separately latched corruption is a pre-existing behavior requiring further audit; 9.2.1 is not treated as a guarantee of immunity from later independent corruption.

spec_interpretations: Section 6.50 selects all registers inferred by a process, not variables lexically below its name. Supported RTL whole-process names come from the outer named body or implicit labeled-statement block; arbitrary nested blocks are not classified as whole processes.

Process expansion followed by physical state/domain intersection is the adopted interpretation of 6.50, consistent with ancestor-instance expansion; the text does not explicitly prescribe expansion order. External processes may infer retained state inside the target domain without assigning retention to outside neighbors.

A label before an outer event control has the same activation proof when its named sequential wrapper contains exactly that timing statement. Work preceding a wait, conditional waits and deeper wrappers retain the unsupported classification.

Section 9.5.3 requires ordinary in-domain state to stay corrupt even when an external procedural writer executes. Until generic per-target issue/epoch lowering is added, referenced external-process origins with final unretained in-domain state are diagnosed before rewrites, including exclusions and higher-precedence no_retention. Initial/Final sources do not create that admission condition.

Virtual/fork/context-DPI or unresolved producer closures remain conservatively unsupported even for exclusions or no_retention selectors. Reference-formal escapes retain explicit unsupported-writer diagnostics.

completed.architecture: Reuse exact-event snapshot registration for the negative edge of the evaluated/published primary NORMAL predicate. Atomically advance the existing domain epoch, clear restoration readiness and write default-corrupt ordinary packed roots, excluding retention-owned storage. Partition payloads below the LLVM integer width limit, placing epoch/restoration in only one group. Startup OFF policy is primed before HDL actors, while ordinary restoration remains after retention updates in the existing monitor. Share explicit callback-capture construction with Balloon lowering. Validate the complete batch before cancelling native/raw-design queued updates or committing any state; notify after all writes. Canonicalize STATIC/GLOBAL aliases with clipped object bounds, mark raw design cancellation using reserved sequence zero, preserve mixed-drain cursor positions and retire cancelled events from calendars/compaction. Backend cancellation-index encoding uses linear BitVector construction rather than quadratic membership scans.
spec_interpretations: A published NORMAL-to-non-NORMAL transition is destructive even if supplies return ON without a process yield. Raw switch controls that never propagate are not published loss. Capture reads evaluated supplies with inline switch prediction disabled.

Initial execution and assignment issue remain exempt under 9.2.1; a subsequent target loss cancels already-queued target updates under 9.5.3, including Initial-issued NBAs. An Initial event issued while OFF retains HDL scheduling if no later target loss occurs. This preserves the agreed separation between issue semantics and separately scheduled target events.

Corruption uses each HDL type default, including X for four-state state and zero for two-state state. Cancellation occurs even when that value is unchanged, and never re-corrupts an exempt Initial write merely because a later periodic monitor executes.

This chunk observes loss exactly and cancels already-issued updates; it does not yet qualify clock activations queued before loss but resumed after restoration. Event-time qualification of those powered-actor activations is a separate immediate prerequisite, including causally later valid clocks.

Domains with owned net drivers retain the existing periodic implementation until resolved contribution targets are supported. Source force/procedural assign/release of new ordinary snapshot roots is diagnosed instead of bypassing LRM precedence or failing later as invalid runtime metadata; unrelated provably distinct AON targets remain supported.

VPI-off compilation can elide unused source-only roots. Executable storage references, storage captures, actual UPF control uses and explicit observability remain live, with independent descriptor namespaces respected. Empty/no-retention intent does not retain unused controls. VPI-enabled and raw MLIR default paths preserve inventory conservatively; waveform use also preserves storage.

The current supply model preserves effectful supply commands until elaboration materializes supply stores; generated switch stores also appear then. The late publication scan therefore covers actual ordinary loss sources without prematurely freezing unused HDL inventory. Future HDL supply linkage or logic-expression power sources must revisit that ordering; Balloon data/control publications keep their early barriers.

completed.architecture: Compiler-only shared ClockSnapshots builds one history/arm and one existing snapshot registration per original repeating event. A first qualified edge disarms even while OFF, freezes actual published NORMAL and domain epoch, and gates the original body before any RHS, helper, blocking write or NBA. spec_interpretations: Pending activation validity depends on the published clock occurrence and intervening exact primary loss, independently of delayed restoration readiness. An edge while OFF cannot become eligible after ON, and later unarmed physical edges cannot relabel a pending occurrence.

HDL iff qualification is sampled using SV truth at the edge; condition-only publications do not trigger. Directed vector edges use the LSB and SV four-state transition table; Change compares every packed bit including X/Z changes. Native single Edge/EdgeIff lowering now preserves full Change width, matching existing Any/bytecode behavior.

Generic whole-body qualification is limited to exact-epoch packed-storage domains. Owned-driver domains retain the prior periodic path. Level/combinational restoration remains separate, and Initial execution remains exempt.

Strategy RTC or retention-supply restrictions do not suppress ordinary neighboring state or unrelated body effects. Balloon priority channels remain independent. Master/slave pending RTC/RET qualification is still deferred and explicitly recorded for the next strategy-event prerequisite.

Existing unsupported computed/managed/mixed-edge contexts remain diagnosed. The original wait operation, continuation operands, site, resume region and repeating metadata are preserved. Direct persistent clock/iff references and static packed views are required.

completed.scope: Exact master/slave retention policy, independent event-qualified clocks, Initial output projection and obsolete future-NBA retirement
completed.architecture: Replace delayed bad/freeze actors, pending-process descriptors, repeated backing monitors, per-register cancellation scans and domain update hooks with bounded compiler-generated policy snapshots. Their pure three-bit summary is writable, destructive and output-enabled; group0 alone records previous policy and epoch. N/Q fields split individually at the LLVM integer limit and all groups sample pre-state. A separate closed initializer applies startup policy once; regular callbacks observe destructive entry, while per-writer master channels share ClockSnapshots history/arm with other strategies and domains. Every admitted normal data write already mirrors/projects Q explicitly or uses existing atomic pair/independent view NBA primitives, so no data-primary monitor is needed. Optional private runtime epoch retirement caches current values by plane pointer, bit count and handle, clears invalid pending halves and preserves borrowed/draining indices. It runs after relevant snapshot commits before notices and once at quiescent future-time selection, avoiding per-actor scans and obsolete deadlines. No public runtime function, ABI/layout field, intrinsic opcode or dialect operation is added.
spec_interpretations: For P=published primary NORMAL, R=retention NORMAL: W=P&&!RTC&&(R||!RET_SUP_COR); B=(RET_SUP_COR&&!R)||(!P&&(!RTC||!R)); Q-enable is R for retention-powered output, otherwise P&&(R||!RET_SUP_COR). Advance epoch once on W falling or B rising. RTC/RET-only invalidity stays per retained target and cannot suppress ordinary neighboring writes or body effects.

Master N corruption is transition based: forced B corruption at startup, then new B entry. An exempt Initial write may replace previously corrupt N, and changing Q output power alone cannot change N lifetime. Both Initial and policy paths project actual N using the same output-power predicate. This interpretation follows the Initial exemption and independent output supply; a later genuine B entry still destroys that initialized value.

RTC entry invalidates earlier issued delayed retained NBAs as the established 9.7.3 precedence interpretation; 9.5.3 explicitly mandates cancellation for destructive corruption. Recoveries, held policy summaries and benign voltage changes do not invalidate events. NO_RET with retention-powered output can change Q visibility while N and its future occurrences remain valid.

All directly executed Initial stores remain exempt at their scheduled times, including delayed Initial execution. Own-state reads use N, Q observes independent output power, and later raw root stores retain their existing support with explicit Q projection. Initial NBAs, opaque/helper/fork writers, mixed/partial functional writers and broader caller-specific or partial captured initialization aliases remain diagnosed.

Obsolete events must not advance final time. Retirement tests only irreversible epoch mismatch, never a temporarily false eligibility observer; checked successful atomic pair decisions remain owned by the pair. Future-time VPI queries observe compiler epoch retirement before snapshot notifications. Arbitrary direct epoch mutations retire at scheduler quiescence, not eagerly during const queue queries.

Snapshot cancellation flags remain absent from master policy registrations because they are unconditional; all admitted functional retained NBAs already carry the exact epochs. Private queue cleanup avoids dead future barriers, adds no ordinary-design persistent state and does not rescan conditions at each actor arbitration.
